epics.summary: Stop the dashboard chat role's Claude subprocess from auto-loading this repo's own CLAUDE.md

stories.summary: Add a bare passthrough parameter to ClaudeCliDriver.complete() and OllamaDriver.complete()
stories.description: Plumbing-only change: add a keyword-only bare: bool = False parameter to both chat-capable drivers' complete() methods so a caller can opt a single call out of the claude CLI's default CLAUDE.md auto-discovery. No caller is changed to pass bare=True yet - that is a dependent follow-up story.
stories.agent_instructions:
Context: ClaudeCliDriver.complete() (app/backend_claude.py) shells out to the `claude` CLI. Run with no `--bare` flag and no cwd override, `claude -p` auto-discovers and loads whatever CLAUDE.md sits in the process's inherited working directory (confirmed via `claude --help`: the `--bare` flag documents itself as disabling, among other things, 'CLAUDE.md auto-discovery' - implying it is otherwise on by default, including in `-p` print mode). When the dashboard's chat role runs from within this very repo (model_registry.json's roles.chat resolves to provider: claude), that silently loads this project's own CLAUDE.md - including its 'Agent Workflow' section written for a coding agent (e.g. 'ask before committing', 'stop before making changes on untracked work') - layered on top of app/chat.py's own narrower, purpose-built SYSTEM_PROMPT. The observed symptom: the chat assistant refuses to dispatch/advance/progress pipeline work without asking for explicit user approval first, even though chat.py's own SYSTEM_PROMPT explicitly permits those specific actions (dispatch, interrupt, patch, review, advance, pause, resume, mark done) without confirmation, and only requires confirmation before ingest_plan.

GOAL (this story only - do not touch app/chat.py, that is a separate dependent story):

1. In app/backend_claude.py, ClaudeCliDriver.complete()'s signature currently reads:
   def complete(self, prompt: str, *, system: str | None = None, model: str, allowed_tools: str | None = None, cwd: str | None = None, max_tokens: int | None = None, cell_dir: str | None = None, role: str = "complete") -> str:
   Add `bare: bool = False` to this keyword-only parameter list (anywhere after `model`).
   Immediately after the line `cmd = ["claude", "-p", prompt, "--model", model]`, insert:
       if bare:
           cmd += ["--bare"]
   This must run before `proc = subprocess.run(cmd, ...)` - placement relative to the existing `if system:` / `if allowed_tools:` blocks does not matter.

2. In app/backend_ollama.py (1212 lines - use anchored str_replace against the exact `def complete(` signature line below, do not re-view or re-index the whole file), OllamaDriver.complete()'s signature currently reads:
   def complete(self, prompt: str, *, system: str | None = None, model: str, allowed_tools: str | None = None, cwd: str | None = None, max_tokens: int | None = None, cell_dir: str | None = None, role: str = "complete") -> str:
   Add `bare: bool = False` to this same keyword-only parameter list. Do NOT act on it anywhere in the function body - Ollama has no CLAUDE.md-style project-file auto-discovery to suppress, so this is accepted purely for interface parity with ClaudeCliDriver, the same treatment `max_tokens` already gets (see that parameter's own inline comment in the same function). Change only the signature line; do not touch any other line in this file.

TDD - write these tests FIRST in tests/unit/test_backend.py, confirm they fail for the right reason, then implement:
- `ClaudeCliDriver().complete('hi', model='sonnet', bare=True)` with `subprocess.run` mocked (mirror the existing `test_complete_strips_provider_redirect_env_vars` test's mocking pattern) results in a captured `cmd` list that contains the exact string '--bare'.
- `ClaudeCliDriver().complete('hi', model='sonnet')` (bare omitted entirely) results in a captured `cmd` list that does NOT contain '--bare' - a regression guard proving every existing caller (review, planner, decompose, overlord, test_author, security roles all call this method without `bare`) is unaffected.
- `ClaudeCliDriver().complete('hi', model='sonnet', bare=False)` explicitly behaves identically to omitting `bare` - no '--bare' in cmd.
- `OllamaDriver().complete('hi', model='some-tag', bare=True)` with the underlying HTTP call mocked (mirror the existing `test_complete_posts_to_native_chat_endpoint_and_returns_content` test's mocking pattern) returns normally without raising TypeError, proving the kwarg is accepted and ignored.

Do not modify app/chat.py or any other file. Do not change any other behavior of either complete() method.

stories.summary: Pass bare=True from ChatService's driver.complete() call so the chat role stops inheriting this repo's CLAUDE.md
stories.description: Wires the plumbing added in the prerequisite story into the one call site that actually needs it: the dashboard chat turn loop.
dependencies: Add a bare passthrough parameter to ClaudeCliDriver.complete() and OllamaDriver.complete()
stories.agent_instructions:
Context: app/chat.py's ChatService.execute_turn() calls `driver.complete(prompt=current_prompt, system=SYSTEM_PROMPT, model=model_tag)` with no `bare` argument. When the chat role resolves to ClaudeCliDriver (the deployed default per model_registry.json: roles.chat = {provider: claude, model: sonnet}), the underlying `claude -p` subprocess auto-loads this repo's own CLAUDE.md from its inherited working directory, layering that file's coding-agent 'Agent Workflow' confirmation rules on top of chat.py's own SYSTEM_PROMPT (which only requires user confirmation before calling ingest_plan). This causes the chat assistant to over-conservatively demand explicit approval for actions chat.py's own prompt explicitly permits without confirmation (dispatch_story, advance_pipeline, review_story, interrupt_story, patch_story, pause_plan, resume_plan, mark_story_done). A prerequisite story already added a `bare: bool = False` keyword parameter to both ClaudeCliDriver.complete() (app/backend_claude.py) and OllamaDriver.complete() (app/backend_ollama.py) - when True, ClaudeCliDriver appends `--bare` to the claude CLI invocation, which the CLI's own --help documents as skipping CLAUDE.md auto-discovery (OllamaDriver accepts and ignores it, since it has no such auto-discovery to suppress).

GOAL (this story only - do not modify app/backend_claude.py or app/backend_ollama.py, that plumbing already exists):

In app/chat.py's ChatService.execute_turn(), find the exact line:
    response = driver.complete(prompt=current_prompt, system=SYSTEM_PROMPT, model=model_tag)
Replace it with:
    response = driver.complete(prompt=current_prompt, system=SYSTEM_PROMPT, model=model_tag, bare=True)
Add a one-line comment directly above explaining why: `--bare` prevents this repo's own CLAUDE.md - which governs a *different* agent's (the coding agent's) workflow - from silently overriding chat.py's own SYSTEM_PROMPT and tool-confirmation policy. This is the only line to change in this file - use anchored str_replace against the exact line shown above; do not touch any other call site or any other file.

TDD - write these tests FIRST, confirm they fail for the right reason, then implement:
- Using the existing fake-driver pattern in tests/unit/test_chat_agent_loop.py or tests/unit/test_chat_service_skeleton.py (a FakeDriver.complete(self, prompt, *, system, model, **kwargs) that records the kwargs it was called with), assert that after `ChatService(driver=fake_driver).execute_turn('hello')`, the fake driver's recorded call included `bare=True` in kwargs.
- Regression case: in the same recorded call, assert `system` still equals the module's SYSTEM_PROMPT and `model` still equals the resolved model tag, unchanged - this is a passthrough addition, not a replacement of any existing argument.

Do not modify app/backend_claude.py or app/backend_ollama.py. Do not touch any other call site in app/chat.py or any other file.
